problem:
The center of the hyperbola $-16{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-8y+32x=16$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-16{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-8y+32x=16 \\ {y}^{2}-8y\,-\,16{x}^{2}+32x & =16 \\ [{y}^{2}-8y]\,-\,16[{x}^{2}-2x] & =16 \\ [(y-4)^{2}-16]\,-\,16\,[(x-1)^{2}-1] & =16 \\ (y-4)^{2}-16\,-\,16(x-1)^{2}+16 & =16 \\ (y-4)^{2}-16(x-1)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{(y-4)^{2}}{16}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{1} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-4)^{2}}{{4}^{2}}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{{1}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,1,4\,).$
